dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: #I looove playing Dodoco's Bomb-Tastic Adventure with you, {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} Honorary Knight and Paimon! Thanks for playing with me.

choices.text: I'm having fun too! One more round!

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Yay, let's go let's go!

choices.text: Should we walk you back home later?

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Oh, right, I can't stay out too late... I'll behave and go home when it's time for bed!

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: But I know my way home! Let's meet back here in the morning!

choices.text: Let's take a break and continue later.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Sure! You don't have to stay here if you have other things to do.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: We still have loads of time, so I'll be waiting for you here during the day if you want to play more!

dialogues.speaker: Ematol
dialogues.text: Let the Wind Lead! Follow the Sparks! Greetings, Great Honorary Knight, and to you, Helper in White. I, Investigative Team Weapons Officer Ematol, am at your service. What can I do for you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: By sparks... could you mean... the Spark Knight?

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: That's right! That's my personal motto!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Out of all the elite warriors of the Knights of Favonius, the most powerful must be our revered and adorable Spark Knight!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: She traverses every inch of Mondstadt with a lively demeanor; and her petite and nimble form carries enough firepower to completely annihilate an entire legion.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: No matter how numerous the enemy force is, they will all be burnt to ashes and scattered by the winds to the sound of the Spark Knight's delightful laughter and rumbling symphony of her "explosives so powerful that they shouldn't exist in the world"!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y—Yeah... and what's with the "shouldn't exist in the world" you mentioned?

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Ah, for that question, you've come to the right person! I'm a pretty skilled alchemist myself...

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Although I'm not nearly as learned as Master Sucrose or Master Timaeus, and so far behind Captain Albedo I can't even see his shadow on a winter's morn, I do have my own expertise and have designed many explosives for engineering use!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: However, their explosive velocity simply isn't in the same league as the Jumpy Dumpty. They are only capable of deflagrating, rather than transitioning to a high brisance detonation...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Deflagration this, detonate this, all Paimon understood was "explosive"!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Oh no! I'm so sorry, I got carried away and didn't do a good enough job explaining, it's all my fault!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Anyway, ordinary explosive materials are two, maybe even two and a half generations away from the masterpieces designed by the Spark Knight! In terms of cost, they aren't even close to the same level either.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: When I asked the Spark Knight about the secret ingredients for Jumpy Dumpty, she only answered:

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: "Jumpy Dumpty's formula was given to Klee by Klee's mother! If there's a secret ingredient, it must be her love for Klee!"

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: But it's understandable for her to say that! Since the formula for such a powerful explosive is something confidential that could affect the balance of power between nations, it's simply above the pay grade of someone as low and insignificant as I!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: All I can do is try to follow in the footsteps of the Spark Knight and try even harder to develop my own formula for explosive materials.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: I will work hard, and strive to achieve my goal, that one day I could make something that's at least... one twentieth as powerful and cost-effective as the Jumpy Dumpty!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Oh, the mere thought of it makes me tremble with excitement... The perfect rate explosive rate, an earth-shattering shockwave, a concise build, and low cost...

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Hehehe... Jumpy Dumpty... Hehehe...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: P—Paimon has never met someone like this... Let's just call her... "Bombaholic" in the future!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Let's get out of here, {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we get a chance, we need to remind Albedo... Pay attention to the Bombaholic on his team, and take care of her mental state!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon has never heard that title before. Sounds impressive.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Indeed! If you don't mind, Great Honorary Knight, please allow me to give you a brief introduction to some of the responsibilities of the investigation team as I understand them...

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: "In addition to basic military intelligence reports, we also investigate, collect, and analyze combat-related data of the Knights, finding ways to continuously improve tactics and combat capabilities."

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Therefore, learning the habits of the Knights and modifying their weapons and equipment are both part of our responsibilities.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: The so-called Weapons Specialist, in truth, is a knight who is responsible for testing experimental weapons.

choices.text: So you must also be a skilled combatant?

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Not at all. I know nothing about combat. If I were to take up a sword, even a wild boar could take on twenty of me.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: But I'm tougher than nails! Haha!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: When I was trying to analyze the formula for Jumpy Dumpty, I went through... Let me count... 27 incidents, and the blast sent me flying in 19 of them!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: But after bandaging myself up and applying splints, I returned to the team's garrison the next day and went back to work!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: My colleagues were very understanding and helped me keep the incidents hidden from Captain Albedo. Otherwise, I would've missed out on work!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Following the Sparks is not for the faint of heart or the undisciplined!

choices.text: You don't have to push yourself that hard...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now Paimon's really worried about this Knight's mental state... If we get a chance, we should ask Albedo to keep an eye on her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Caring about nothing but your work is a bit much!

choices.text: You could've asked your Captain for some leave...
Are you also a Master of Weaponry?
Why are you squirming like that?

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Oh! It just that the Great Honorary Knight and The Helper in White are so concerned about my work... It's exciting! But it almost makes me quite nervous...

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Great Honorary Knight, Ematol, Weapons Specialist of the Investigation Team reporting in! Currently executing an urgent mission: Annihilate the Invasive Anglers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! You became so formal all of a sudden. Are we really held in such high regard in the Knights of Favonius?

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Huh? You haven't heard about it, Great Honorary Knight? it must be because you've been so busy lately. Such things aren't important enough to warrant your attention!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: It's quite simple, actually. Not long ago, a merchant from Sumeru came here on business and "released" a few Anglers in Cider Lake...

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Anglers are a type of fish native to Sumeru and have basically no natural predators in the waters of Mondstadt. This means they can multiply quickly and take over the lake, leaving little room for other species of fish to survive.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: After evaluating the issue, the Knights of Favonius assigned Phonia and me to handle it.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: If you happen to encounter another knight from the investigation team on the other side of the lake, that would be Phonia. She's operating, uh, "that one detection device," an alchemical device developed by Captain Albedo...

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: I don't remember the exact name, but it can detect underwater creatures and identify the unique bodyshape of the Anglers.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: As for me, my job is to deploy bombs at precise locations to annihilate these bullying invasive species and restore peace to Cider Lake.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Impressive, isn't it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right... Paimon was just gonna say, Klee's an expert at that.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: No, no, absolutely not! We cannot trouble the Spark Knight with such a mundane task! The Spark Knight's time is incredibly valuable and should only be allocated according to her own will!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Besides, it's not like the Great Honorary Knight often... "uses heavy naval cannons to blow up pigeons"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you did that, not even a single feather would remain! That's definitely going way too far!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: That's what I mean! The Spark Knight's bombs are like heavy naval cannons, and those schools of Anglers are little different from flocks of pigeons.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: But our objective happens to be "eliminating the pigeons without harming the finches beside them." That's why I am the perfect man for the job.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Although the submarine bombs I use are imitations of the Spark Knight's Jumpy Dumpty, they are only one tenth as strong.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: With the help of specially designed detonators and the positions provided by Phonia, I can guarantee that the Angler nesting grounds are demolished without harming any native fish species in Cider Lake!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon gets it now... You want to target and eliminate only those fish, without harming any others.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Great! That means it was a good analogy! Of course, the pigeons have done nothing wrong. I just wanted you to know how powerful the Spark Knight's weapons are!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: However, it is not yet time for me to start. Phonia hasn't completed her preliminary recon work, and doing anything rash right now would surely startle them...

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: But Phonia is maddeningly slow, and she has a bad temper. Every time I get close to her, she starts complaining about how I'm messing up her equipment and making her go deaf.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: I don't dare to rush her... But if this keeps up, just when will I finally be able to sail in my dear little boat and drop my beloved bombs...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't let me keep you!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: You're too kind! Great Honorary Knight and The Helper in White, please take care!

choices.text: What did the pigeons ever do to you...?

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Oh! My analogy doesn't seem to be fitting... I'll have to come up with a better one next time. Anyway, I have nothing against the pigeons. I just wanted you to know how powerful the Spark Knight's weapons are!

dialogues.speaker: Phonia
dialogues.text: Honorary Knight, and The Helper in White. Phonia of the Investigation Team, reporting. We're currently carrying out an urgent mission: Annihilate the Invasive Anglers. I am in charge of acoustic recon.

dialogues.speaker: Phonia
dialogues.text: If you have any questions, there is a knight called Ematol by the lake. She's better at interpersonal communication and can provide you with detailed information.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: R—Right! We just wanted to greet you, and you just started babbling on...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Feels like she's a bit impatient...)

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Isn't that a good thing? We all work for the Knights of Favonius, and we're all on the clock right now, so we should not indulge ourselves in meaningless gossip but the exchange of useful information...

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Besides, I'm just a common "cog" while you are the heroes who have "saved Mondstadt" on your resumes. Someone like me is not worth much of your precious time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, that's a bit offensive! We're not the type to... use people and treat them as tools!

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Oh, I'm sorry for the misunderstanding. A "cog" is simply how I define myself.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: I am just an ordinary person with no talent. I have neither the capability nor the determination to take charge. The only role I'm fit to play on the stage of the machine that is the Knights of Favonius is that of a "cog."

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Or you can also call me a "pawn" or "gear"... I don't mind.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Putting it like that is totally heartless!

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Heartless? I actually find it to my liking.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: There's no need for me to overthink anything or do things according to my own will. I simply do what my superior says. Get to work on time, and leave on time. Life is simple.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: There's a rumor going around that says: "In emergency situations the Honorary Knight has command authority on the front lines equivalent to a captain." Who knows, I may have the chance to be temporarily assigned to your unit in the future.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Of course, every situation is different, and every task has a different priority. We are currently not in any such critical sitaution, so I can just focus on the "Annihilate the Invasive Anglers" task that I've been assigned.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: As such, I must ask you two to keep some distance from me while I work. Both my equipment and I require a quiet working environment.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: You certainly wouldn't want some "cogs" to malfunction and affect the entire "machine," would you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph! Paimon rarely sees a knight so willing to close the door and leave the world behind! Or maybe... they're a "heartless workaholic"!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #C'mon {NICKNAME}! Let's leave her here to do her work all alone!

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: I just told you the most important information, but as it seems that's not enough for you. I'll supplement it with a few more words.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: I am Phonia, a member of the intelligence division of the investigation team. Though I have served for 6 years, I have only carried out 67 battlefield support ops and 31 direct action ops.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: My greatest martial accomplishment was defeating 1 Hilichurl Brute, 2 Hilichurl Shamans, and a few Hilichurl Shooters, with Ematol using simple roadside explosives, mopping up a small area of the forest...

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: As you can see, the gap in combat capability between me and you, Honorary Knight, is as wide as that between a boar and Stormterror. Perhaps you will simply forget about an unimportant, ordinary knight like me in a couple days.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's going on? Why are you suddenly... giving us a work report? So serious...

choices.text: There's no need to be so tense...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Yeah! Even though {NICKNAME} is an Honorary Knight, we're not on duty now! Just relax!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We're always meeting all kinds of people in the wilderness, and it's really great when we talk and talk and end up becoming friends!

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: I see. You wish to dicuss personal matters. Let me think...

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: I'm Phonia, 26 years old, single. I currently live in the third room on the third floor of the third building to the right of the city gates. I have a roommate who's also my tenant called Ematol, and the monthly rent is... I forget, it's not important.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: My hobby is to sleep. After work, I just go home and sleep. If it's too noisy, I'll have some wine to help me sleep. I don't remember what kind of wine I used to drink, but that's not important either. As long as it can get me drunk, it's good wine.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Sometimes I stay at the secret camp near Dragonspine temporarily in accord with Captain Albedo's orders. I like it there because it's quiet, so I can have a good sleep without anyone disturbing me.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: That's a valid point. A quiet environment and high-quality sleep are beneficial for my work. After all, my exceptional hearing is my most valuable skill.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Paimon feels like this knight... is incredible at killing conversations! Paimon doesn't know how to respond...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (And she keeps going on about her interests, which are still related to work... Paimon gonna give her a nickname... The "Silent Workaholic"!)

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Thanks, The Helper in White. That's a good nickname. If we ever need a callsign in the team, I'll use that.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Honorary Knight and The Helper in White, if you do not require further information from me... then please excuse the Silent Workaholic to resume her recon work.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y—You... You go ahead. We'll leave you to it!

choices.text: Is your personal life that... mechanical, too?

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Hmm... You're the first one to point out my life is machine-like. I think that's great, living a routine life keeps me away from trouble.

choices.text: Just think of us as new friends...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It sounds impressive... but it looks like you're just standing by the lake, not moving a muscle? Paimon doesn't see any equipment around, either.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Good topic, Honorary Knight and The Helper in White. You have noticed how compact Captain Albedo's handcrafted equipment is. Hostiles won't be any to spot it either in the future!

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: I have already deployed the recon equipment's active unit underwater. It utilizes a special wave... Anyway, it surveys the nearby area with the help of Hydro.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: I'm wearing the unit's receiver in my ears, and it's about the size of regular earplugs. The detection signal of the active unit is transmitted directly to me.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: With these sound signals, I am able to analyze the locations of all Anglers and lock onto their nests by plotting their path and information on the map. Then, Ematol can come in and eradicate them in one go.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That amazing?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's almost like magic!

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Truly incredible alchemical creations appear no different from magic to the untrained eye. When other technologies reach a certain maturity, similar high-level creations will also be created.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: For example, I heard Fontaine manufactures large volumes of clockwork tech-based... humanoid machines. They can even take on the responsibility of defending the city. That also seems like magic to me.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: But I digress... Anyway, according to Captain Albedo, after a few discussions with Jean and the other captains, they reached a consensus...

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: "The combat capabilities of the Knights of Favonius must be steadily improved with the minimum budget."

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Yeah. The intermittent reports from the expedition team have given us a clearer picture of our far away enemies. Some are just too powerful for our knights to handle effectively at their current skill level.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: The Knights of Favonius must continue to improve, striving for zero casualties and minimal resource consumption while eradicating potential invaders of Mondstadt and protecting everyone. For this purpose, there are no standards that are too high.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But how is that related to what you're doing now...? Like this "Annihilate the Invasive Anglers" operation?

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Good question, Helper in White. To put it simply, the conclusion from the meeting at that time was "information."

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: The most cost efficient way to improve is by enhancing the knights' ability to acquire information, allowing them to gain the initiative on the battlefield and engage enemies from a more advantageous positions at the proper time.

choices.text: I see! So you're testing out new equipment!

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: I'm impressed, Honorary Knight. Communicating with you is indeed efficient and straightforward.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: My job in the investigation team, a Signals Officer, and the equipment I'm using, are some of the earliest products of the Knights of Favonius' plan to improve our combat capabilities.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: The equipment shares similar design principles with the survey device Captain Albedo provided Mika with. This one has better battery life, increased accuracy against small targets, and is more convenient to use.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: As one of the first Signals Officers trained to use this equipment, I am responsible for being a military instructor, training a large cohort of Signals Officers for the frontline.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Ideally, a few Signals Officers will be assigned to each platoon. They will use detection equipment to acquire information about enemies while they are still distant, allowing them to utilize the intelligence to deploy the most advantageous tactics.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now Paimon's lost... Why make something as simple as a fight so complicated!? When we see enemies, we prefer the hands-on approach and just go at them...

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: You are heroes. We are cannon fodder. We're different.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: To avoid being cannon fodder torn to pieces by heroes like you, we regular knights have to actually use our brains. At least... we put some distance between us before you come charging over.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Being easily trampled on isn't acceptable. We knights are tasked with the protection of Mondstadt. We can't afford to be reckless.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! How can you say something so demoralizing with a straight face!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, you've got a point. We never considered that... The opponents we've defeated might actually be warriors, who actually trained hard every day...

choices.text: Warriors must have the dignity of a warrior!

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Thank you for the encouragement, and for taking notice of a regular knight like me. I hope to one day fight by your side.

choices.text: Carry on with the testing, Signals Officer!
I still don't get what it has to do with you...

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Perhaps I talked too much about the nature of the issue, which might be too broad... Back to the topic at hand, I am testing new equipment.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Yes. We are currently at peace, so before the Knights of Favonius approve any military-related budget, we have to consider the impact on the civilians. Our citizens' needs come first, and we can use what's left for military improvements.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Under such conditions, Mora must be spent only when necessary. Therefore, we need to verify which aspects to enhance that will bring about the highest improvement on overall combat capabilities.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Take care! If you encounter the others, please remind them to keep a low profile. Thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Helga
dialogues.text: Hello, Great Hero of Mondstadt! I am Helga, a deliveryperson for Good Hunter. How may I help you?

response.speaker: Helga
response.text: Yeah. I deliver orders for the restaurant. It's a super simple but enjoyable job!

response.speaker: Helga
response.text: Some customers don't want to cook from scratch or need to host important guests at home, so they place orders in advance, and the restaurant sends us to deliver the meal orders to the designated location.

response.speaker: Helga
response.text: Really? You think so? But I find it pretty enjoyable myself!

response.speaker: Helga
response.text: No matter when or where, we allow people to easily enjoy their favorite foods... Delivering happiness like this gives me a sense of fulfillment and achievement!

response.speaker: Helga
response.text: A few years ago, I accidentally fell and broke my leg. I had to stay at home and could barely get out of bed.

response.speaker: Helga
response.text: Usually, I'm the one who cooks at home since my dad's a terrible cook. His food is so bad even he can't stomach it. Moreover, he gets home pretty late, so the nearby restaurants are all closed by then.

response.speaker: Helga
response.text: During that time, my dad and I relied on the food delivered by deliverypeople! The moment we heard knocking on the door, we knew our hunger would be satisfied!

response.speaker: Helga
response.text: That's why I signed up as soon as I recovered. I decided to become the fastest, and the most reliable food deliveryperson, bringing my customers their satisfying meals!

response.speaker: Helga
response.text: #I heard there was once a deliveryperson nicknamed the "Golden Shadow." No matter how demanding the orders were or how great the distance, {M#he}{F#she} could deliver them in record time!

response.speaker: Helga
response.text: Sadly, the Golden Shadow was a temporary worker hired by the restaurant from the Adventurers' Guild and only stayed a few days, leaving only the legend of their speed.

response.speaker: Helga
response.text: #{M#He}{F#She}'s an inspiration to me. I also want to become that kind of... well, a top deliveryperson in all of Teyvat!

response.speaker: Helga
response.text: Thanks for the encouragement! Now I feel motivated!

choices.text: Is that so? Keep it up!
Doing the same job over and over can't be enjoyable...

response.speaker: Helga
response.text: Oh, right! Sara said that the Good Hunter has received a special order to deliver food to the Spark Knight at regular times.

response.speaker: Helga
response.text: So she won't forget to eat her lunch while she's on important missions.

response.speaker: Helga
response.text: Seeing the Spark Knight playing games so carelessly and happily... Ahem! I mean, executing important missions, I'm happy to be of help!

response.speaker: Helga
response.text: A colleague of mine isn't so lucky. She received an order and had to deliver the food to somewhere near one of the cliffs near the <color=#00E1FFFF>Brightcrown Mountains</color>...

response.speaker: Helga
response.text: Delivering food around Mondstadt is tiring enough, but to think she had to go across mountains and rivers carrying the backpack...

response.speaker: Helga
response.text: Fortunately, the customer is a wealthy merchant who always tips well...

response.speaker: Helga
response.text: She could have delivered dozens of orders and earned days worth of wages in the time it takes to make the trip otherwise...

choices.text: Don't let me keep you. Later!

response.speaker: Helga
response.text: Take care, you two. Drop by the Good Hunter whenever you're free and treat yourselves to a great meal!

dialogues.speaker: Ematol
dialogues.text: Teeheehee! What a wonderfully executed mission! Perhaps... the Captain will allow me to write the training manual when we create a "bomb squad"!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Judging from how proudly you're talking to yourself, the mission must be going swimmingly?

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Oh! Great Honorary Knight and The Helper in White, I'm happy to report that the mission to "Annihilate the Invasive Anglers" has been completed!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Phonia has double-checked and confirmed that I have cleared out all the Angler nests. Not a single fish slipped through our net!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: However, there were a few nests that were quite tough. I had to use multiple bombs to get rid of them. The heavy rocks were really difficult to deal with.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: No wonder all the Spark Knight's bombs, large or small, have such a high ratio of explosive charge to weight! It's all about ensuring sufficient detonation pressure to crack hardened targets! She is so incredible!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great. More technobabble that we can't understand...

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: However, strictly speaking, charge quantity isn't the answer to everything. The primary issue is that explosive energy disperses in every direction and is not focused in a single direction.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Could a cone-shaped casing be used to concentrate the explosive energy so it would penetrate thick defenses...?

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Then a cone-shaped case like that would have to be made of sturdy metal... That's something I need to research...

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Right! With the extra bonus from this operation and a week's salary, I'll treat the Spark Knight to a few grand meals to thank her for her contributions to the operation...

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: And also discuss with her how to make a type of bomb with a new structure that can focus the explosive energy... Heheheh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! It's great that you want to treat Klee to a meal, but you're the one who did all the work.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wouldn't you feel you did all that work for nothing if you just give away everything that you earned through your own hard work and time to others?

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Nothing of the sort! Everything I know about bombs, I either learned from the Spark Knight or I was inspired by her to invent it myself!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: If the Spark Knight hadn't shown me her bombs and explained so much about them, I'd still be... a regular knight without neither strength of arm nor skill with a blade.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: And I wouldn't have been able to complete the mission this time!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: That's why I honestly feel the credit for the success of this mission belongs to the Spark Knight! The Spark Knight is not interested in Mora, but she's definitely into food!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: W—Wow! Such irrefutable, solid logic!

choices.text: Woohoo! The Spark Knight has a new apprentice!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Shh! It's not like that, really!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: The Spark Knight shall always be completely free. A bond like that between master and apprentice, that would be a constraint upon the Spark Knight! I do not wish to impose such trouble on her!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: At most I'll just... Well... Observe the Spark Knight from afar and study how she crafts and deploys bombs...

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Right! Just treat me as a copycat bombmaker in the wild!

choices.text: Woohoo! Klee's student's going to pay for the meal!
You jumped to that topic way too quickly!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Ematol, Weapons Specialist of the investigation team, reporting to the Great Honorary Knight and The Helper in White!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: You may have heard of me, but since you're captain-level heroes who've seen many knights, so it's understandable if you don't remember me!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: If you don't mind, please allow me to give you a brief introduction to some of my responsibilities in the investigation team...

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: "In addition to basic military intelligence reports, we also investigate, collect, and analyze combat-related data of the Knights, finding ways to continuously improve tactics and combat capabilities."

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Therefore, learning the habits of the Knights and modifying their weapons and equipment are both part of our responsibilities.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: The so-called Weapons Specialist, in truth, is a knight who is responsible for testing experimental weapons.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: I was sent to carry out the mission to "Annihilate the Invasive Anglers." I am happy to report that I have successfully eradicated all the invasive Anglers in Cider Lake, and have had the chance to test out a prototype bomb...

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: I am completely satisfied!

choices.text: So you must also be a skilled combatant?

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Not at all. I know nothing about combat. If I were to take up a sword, even a wild boar could take on twenty of me.

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: But I'm tougher than nails! Haha!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: When I was trying to analyze the formula for Jumpy Dumpty, I went through... Let me count... 27 incidents, and the blast sent me flying in 19 of them!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: But after bandaging myself up and applying splints, I returned to the team's garrison the next day and went back to work!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: My colleagues were very understanding and helped me keep the incidents hidden from Captain Albedo. Otherwise, I would've missed out on work!

response.speaker: Ematol
response.text: Following the Sparks is not for the faint of heart or the undisciplined!

choices.text: You don't have to push yourself that hard...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now Paimon's really worried about this Knight's mental state... If we get a chance, we should ask Albedo to keep an eye on her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Caring about nothing but your work is a bit much!

choices.text: You could've asked your Captain for some leave...
Are you also a Master of Weaponry?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (She's obviously too happy to care about anything else... Let's just leave her be...)

dialogues.speaker: Phonia
dialogues.text: Honorary Knight, and The Helper in White. Phonia of the Investigation Team, reporting. We just completed carrying out an urgent mission called "Annihilate the Invasive Anglers," and are now returning to camp.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: It went smoothly. The threat has been completely eliminated. You can rest easy.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Do you have any further instructions?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Th—That's so formal, like she's reporting to a senior officer. Should we also act the part?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "*ahem*... Good job, Signals Officer Phonia! Please be sure to share what you've learned from this experience with the other knights!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Like that?

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Thank you for your approval, Helper in White. However, it may be too difficult for me to effectively teach my colleagues based on this experience.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Although the operation of this detection equipment has already been greatly simplified, it still is beyond the capability of people who with weaker spatial cognition to operate.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: During operation, the jumbled signals from targets of similar sizes, as well as environmental noise and interference, can all easily overwhelm the user in a torrent of information.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Forget about training the rest of the platoon, even just training the other Signals Officers to be familiar with its operations would be a gargantuan task requiring significant time...

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: If it is to become standard equipment, it requires further improvements to make it more accessible, even at the cost of performance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Cognition? Standard equipment... Accessibility...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y—You lost Paimon again!

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: The details don't matter. Anyway, I am not complaining to you two but objectively analyzing the current situation.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: All I can say is, Captain Albedo's minimum requirement of meeting "1/3 of Mika's spatial cognition and anti-interference capabilities" is still too much to ask.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: In any case, I will continue to help improve this piece of equipment until it is suitable for becoming standardized equipment or proven to be unsuitable.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Once a relatively mature prototype is produced... Would you two like to try it?

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: With it, you can confirm distant targets without visual contact. If you have any ways to... attack enemies at range, you can launch a preemptive attack and gain a tactical advantage.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Th—That incredible?

choices.text: We could detect targets far away?

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: No worries. By changing the Alchemy Potion used in the core, this equipment can detect the energy fluctuations of different elements.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: For example, when using an Anemo Potion to detect targets, it can accurately detect targets like Hilichurl Brutes within a range three times greater than the a regular bow's attack range within Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: In situations like that, top archers like Amber the Outrider would be able to conduct "non-line-of-sight shooting" in groups and continuously adjust their firing angle based on observation reports from allies with higher vantage points.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: The enemies might never see the attack coming, and would already been turned into Wolfhooks by their arrows before they figured out what was happening.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When you put it that way, it sounds amazing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME} doesn't usually use a bow. {M#He}{F#She} just charges straight into enemies and beats them up... or sometimes just gets bombarded by those Ruin Guards from a distance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Though it's kind of maddening, Paimon has to admit that sometimes... being able to attack at range really does have a lot of advantages!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: From just how far away could Amber hit a target if she was using such miraculous equipment? Even Paimon's really looking forward to finding out!

choices.text: But it can only be used underwater... That seems a bit limiting...

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: You may already have heard of this mission and heard my briefing, but were likely too busy to have paid it much attention...

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: So allow me to briefly introduce it once more—

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: A certain merchant "released" some Anglers, native to Sumeru, into Cider Lake, which then began to multiply rapidly.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: To prevent these invasive creatures from impacting the water quality of Cider Lake and affecting Mondstadt's wine industry, the Knights of Favonius dispatched a unit with strong recon capabilities to undertake a limited operation.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: I, Signals Officer Phonia of the Investigative Team, and my colleague Weapons Specialist Ematol, received orders to use limited force to precisely eliminate the invasive species with minimal collateral damage.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Currently, Ematol and I have deployed 457 bombs and cleared out 203 nests and all the invasive Anglers, successfully eliminating the negative effects resulting from the introduction of the invasive species.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: According to the calculations of other colleagues, it will take about a week for the residual explosive remnants in the water to fall to safe levels.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: S—Such precise numbers!

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Thank you for your approval.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: This operation has also allowed me to verify a large quantity of information necessary to the development of the Signals Officer corps. As a cog in the Knights of Favonius' grand machine, I have reaped significant benefits.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Goodbye to both of you.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: If there's a chance, I hope I can show you the results of the improved equipment in the near future.

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: *whimper* *sob*

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: How could this happen... I'm not malicious... I never meant for any of this to happen...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What happened to you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You don't look like you're from Mondstadt. Why are you standing here all alone and crying? Did you run into trouble?

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: Oh... Hello...

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: I just left the Knights of Favonius headquarters... I was given a huge fine and a lecture...

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: Though the Knights were all polite and nice, and they just patiently explained everything to me... I still feel so bad about what I did and regret it so much!

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: I... I did a bad thing without thinking... by releasing them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Releasing?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Releasing... It doesn't sound like a bad thing... But it does sound a bit familiar...

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: I once thought... releasing animals, such an act of kindness, the more you do it, the better, but now I know I was wrong, oh so wrong...

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: I am a merchant from Sumeru... A friend of mine who went to Fontaine told me of a secret that's only known to a selected few...

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: "Before doing something important, release some animals into the wild. It will bring you good fortune. Some even buy animals just to release them..."

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: So I released a few Sumeru-native Anglers into Cider Lake before going to my business meeting.

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: I didn't know the Anglers had no natural enemies in Cider Lake and were multiplying so quickly, almost to the point of destroying the lake's ecosystem...

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: Fortunately, the Knights of Mondstadt are capable and reliable. They handled it before it got out of control. Otherwise... Otherwise, I'd have become a villain, condemned by history for all time to come!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So it was you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... But you didn't know what you were doing... You didn't do it intentionally and you've already been punished for it... So, Paimon shouldn't criticize you any more...

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: O—Of course it was never my intention to harm Mondstadt! I've always felt Mondstadt is a really great country!

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: The fact I've been able to become a merchant trading between nations is all thanks to a student from Mondstadt who studied at the Akademiya...

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: A few years ago, before she returned to her home, she entrusted me with the distribution of a game she developed called Shroomsplosion. It became a hit, and earned me substantial capital, which became my startup fund.

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: Mondstadters really are incredibly friendly. They didn't treat me very harshly, even though I made such a big mess...

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: There was a little girl in red who saw me crying by the road, and she even comforted me with lots of snacks...

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: Though the fine itself was huge to me, it merely covered the losses incurred and the salaries of the knights sent to do damage control...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, as long as you can learn from your mistakes. The issue has been resolved, so you don't have to be so hard on yourself now!

choices.text: Just don't go randomly releasing creatures again!

response.speaker: Jala
response.text: Of course! I will remember this lesson! Always!

response.speaker: Jala
response.text: Perhaps... I should donate another shipment to Mondstadt... and then go apologize in person to those Mondstadters who were affected by my actions...

choices.text: And remember to tell your friends that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You really aren't bad at all...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Looks like Miss Jala really was discovered by the Knights of Favonius.

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you two! We meet again!

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: I... I told you about releasing animals before, right? ...Don't ever do it!

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: When I returned to Mondstadt to ask about the local specialties, two knights immediately arrested me at the gates!

dialogues.speaker: Jala

dialogues.speaker: Jala

dialogues.text: We meet again...

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you two!

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: I'm sorry! When I mentioned releasing the fish, I should have gotten down on my knees and admitted my terrible mistake...

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: I had no idea the Anglers I released had no natural enemies in Cider Lake and were multiplying so quickly, almost to the point of destroying the lake's ecosystem!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Uh... Um... You did do something bad to Mondstadt... But why are you apologizing to us?

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: Because I caused you a lot of trouble too! You had to come all this way just to arrest me... It must be exhausting carrying me back to Mondstadt!

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: If only I had come to my senses earlier and willingly gone back to Mondstadt to give myself up... Wait, no, if only I realized what I had done the moment I released them and just turned myself in to the Knights of Favonius...

dialogues.speaker: Jala
dialogues.text: Then I wouldn't have cost you so much time and effort... and the Knights of Favonius wouldn't have had to mobilize so many people to investigate.

choices.text: You're admitting your guilt and showing remorse quite sincerely!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you hadn't believed those rumors and refrained from releasing the fish in the first place, we wouldn't be in this mess...

response.speaker: Jala
